Return the first or last rows of a mobyData

Source: R/mobyData.R
head.mobyData.Rd

head() and tail() behave as they do for any data frame: they return the first (or last) n rows of the detection table for inspection. They return a plain data.frame, so the rows print as rows - the study metadata summary is what print() on the mobyData itself is for.

To subset a dataset and keep it a mobyData (metadata and all), use [ instead: x[1:100, ].

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mobyData'
head(x, n = 6L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mobyData'
tail(x, n = 6L, ...)

Arguments

x

A mobyData object.

n

Number of rows. Defaults to 6, as for utils::head.

...

Further arguments passed to utils::head / utils::tail.

Value

A data.frame of the first (or last) n rows.

See also

as_moby, mobyMeta

Examples

data(rays)
head(rays, 3)      # rows, like any data frame
#>    ID            datetime station    lon    lat            species  receiver
#> 1 D01 2023-04-08 15:05:10    ST03 -8.996 38.456 Dasyatis pastinaca VR2W-1003
#> 2 D01 2023-04-08 15:14:59    ST03 -8.996 38.456 Dasyatis pastinaca VR2W-1003
#> 3 D01 2023-04-08 15:52:10    ST03 -8.996 38.456 Dasyatis pastinaca VR2W-1003
#>      transmitter             timebin
#> 1 A69-1602-30005 2023-04-08 15:00:00
#> 2 A69-1602-30005 2023-04-08 15:00:00
#> 3 A69-1602-30005 2023-04-08 15:00:00
dim(rays[1:100, ]) # '[' keeps the mobyData class and its metadata
#> [1] 100   9
